A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete, readable main text and Appendices A–B. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the algorithms, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original privacy-attack experiments on eight imbalanced datasets in Section 5, including numerical outcomes in Tables 3–4 and reconstruction experiments in Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments on eight datasets and their reported attack-performance outcomes in Section 5, Tables 3–4, and Figures 2–3.

M1.justification: Algorithms 2–3 retain the same DistinSMOTE collinearity-pruning and ReconSMOTE line-intersection procedures, including their inputs, outputs, neighbor searches, and filtering rules.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight datasets and binary classification tasks listed in Table 2, covering the same augmented-data and synthetic-data scenarios. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains naive distinguishing and classifier-based membership inference comparisons. Table 4 retains linkability-based naive metrics and GroundHog membership inference. Comparator membership is unchanged within each experiment.

E3.justification: Section 5 retains the same train/test splits, target selection, metrics, 200-classifier membership-inference setup, and GroundHog setup using 400 training and 200 testing SMOTE models. The imbalance-ratio sweep is also unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the real-versus-augmented membership-inference control and reconstruction recall sweep in Figure 3. Appendix B contains the same analyses of imbalance ratio, neighborhood size, and neighbor mutuality in Figures 4–6.

E5.justification: The reported repetition counts, target averaging, and uncertainty displays are unchanged, including 25 SMOTE generations for each proposed attack and the same ± reporting in Tables 1, 3, and 4. No statistical procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and plotted findings match throughout both PDFs. Tables 3–4 retain average membership-inference AUCs of 0.68 on augmented data and 0.93 on synthetic data, and ReconSMOTE average precision of 1.00 and recall of 0.85. Appendix curves also match.

T1.justification: Assumptions 1–4, Theorems 1–4, Lemmas 1–2, and their proofs are unchanged. This includes the approximate Poisson recall bound in Section 4.3 and the exact Binomial and mutuality analysis in Appendix A.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about the first systematic SMOTE privacy study, the two proposed attacks, theoretical guarantees, and disproportionate exposure of minority records. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The geometric explanations, interpretations of imbalance and privacy leakage, and limitations concerning continuous data and evaluation of original SMOTE remain unchanged. Section 6 also retains the same discussion of SMOTE variants and future evaluation of privacy-preserving variants.

D1.justification: Section 5 retains the imblearn/sklearn implementation information, Apple M4 hardware with 24GB RAM, runtime estimates, and statement promising attack-code release with the final paper. No implementation or code/data-access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 62 references are retained, with unchanged novelty and research-positioning arguments. The new ICLR 2026 footnote updates the paper's publication status.

P1.justification: v2 changes the author's contact email from a UCL address to a SAS address and adds an ICLR 2026 publication and citation note. The scientific prose, terminology, and section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 makes the title and figure/table caption labels bold, adjusts caption spacing, and reflows the opening pages around the added footnote. Figures, tables, and algorithms retain their content, structure, and order.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies updated contact and publication information with minor typographic and pagination changes. The experimental evidence, theoretical arguments, appendix analyses, limitations, and reproducibility information are unchanged. These editorial updates do not establish a meaningful overall gain or loss in paper quality.
